info.name: Indexia Finance — Location Master API
info.description:
Relational Location Master: Continent → Country → State → City → Pincode.

22 ADMIN endpoints (need the admin JWT) under /api/admin/masters/location
 6 PUBLIC endpoints (no token, used by the loan forms) under /api/masters/location

RUN ORDER
  1. Admin — Auth (run first)        saves {{adminToken}} + a fresh {{runId}}
  2. Admin — Overview                the counts-only landing payload
  3. Continents → Countries → States → Cities → Pincodes   (ids chain forward)
  4. Admin — Delete (cleanup)        removes exactly what this run created
  5. Public — no token               works after the cleanup too: it carries its own
                                     activeCountryId / activeStateId chain

SAFE ON ANY DATABASE
Every created record is named "Test … {{runId}}", so re-running never clashes with real or imported data and the cleanup only deletes this run's rows. Needs no environment selected — {{baseUrl}} and the admin credentials are collection variables.

Pincode validity: 3 to 10 digits, stored as a STRING. Duplicate = 409. Missing/inactive parent = 404/400.

TIP: run `npm run import:location` once (19,097 pincodes) and the PUBLIC folder has real data to resolve.

FLAT TABLE: GET /pincodes/table (request 15) returns every pincode with its city / state / country names already joined on, server-paginated and searchable — use it when the panel needs ONE table instead of a five-step cascade.

item.name: Admin — Auth (run first)
item.description: Saves {{adminToken}} for every admin folder and mints a unique {{runId}} for this run.

request.description: Seeded admin: admin@indexiafinance.com / Admin@123 (scripts/seedAdmin.js). Response token is saved to {{adminToken}} automatically.
GET /api/admin/masters/location — the Location Master landing payload. Returns ONLY the 5 counters, never the records, so it stays cheap no matter how many pincodes exist.
GET .../continents — list every continent. Same list shape for all 5 levels.
POST .../continents — body { name, status? }. status defaults to active. Duplicate name (case-insensitive) = 409. Saves {{continentId}}.

PATCH .../continents/:id — only the fields you send are touched. Empty body = 400 "Nothing to update".

WARNING: keep a PARENT on status "active" during a full run. Setting it to inactive/coming_soon makes every child POST below answer 400 "Continent … is coming soon — activate it before adding countries." (that guard is the feature). Status changes are demonstrated on the leaf pincode instead.

query.description: digits match the pincode prefix (400), text matches city OR state name (mumbai, goa)

request.description:
GET .../pincodes/table — ONE flat, server-paginated, searchable table of every pincode with its city / state / country names already joined on, so the panel does not have to chain five cascade calls.

Faster than the cascade: names are resolved in bulk (3 indexed reads per page, not per row), and text search is resolved to city/state ids before the pincode query runs.

Response adds totalPages on top of the usual envelope. Invalid ids -> 400, unknown state/city is NOT an error here (the table simply stays scoped).
POST .../pincodes — { pincode, cityId, prefix?, status? }. NEVER send stateId: it is derived from the city. pincode must be 3-10 digits and is stored as a String. Saves {{pincodeId}}.
PATCH .../pincodes/:id — { pincode?, prefix?, status? }. coming_soon still resolves in the admin UI but is not what the public lookup treats as serviceable for a new application.

item.name: Admin — Delete (cleanup, run last)
item.description:
The 5 remaining admin endpoints. Run this folder LAST: it deactivates then permanently removes the test tree created above.

Reverse order on purpose — a parent with live children answers 409 unless you pass ?force=true, which cascades the soft delete over the whole subtree.

SAFETY: these requests only ever touch the ids this run created, so a populated/imported database is never at risk.

request.description: DELETE .../pincodes/:id — no flags = SOFT delete: status becomes inactive, the row itself is never removed. The public lookup stops returning it immediately.
DELETE .../cities/:id?force=true&hard=true — try it WITHOUT force first to see the 409 guard: "City \"…\" has N pincodes — pass ?force=true to delete them too."
DELETE .../states/:id?force=true&hard=true — cities and their pincodes go with it.
DELETE .../countries/:id?force=true&hard=true.

item.name: P6. Validate pincode for the chosen city

exec: if (json.data) console.log("that pincode really belongs to:", json.data.city + ", " + json.data.state);

request.description:
POST /api/masters/location/pincode/validate — the applicant has State → City selected and typed a pincode. This checks whether that pincode really belongs to the chosen place.

Body: { pincode, state, city } — names or relational (stateId, cityId). Optional strict:true.

ALWAYS HTTP 200 for a well-formed request — read `valid`, not the status:
  { success: true,  valid: true,  message: "Pincode verified successfully", data: {…} }
  { success: false, valid: false, message: "Pincode \"403001\" belongs to Goa — not Karnataka. Please provide a correct pincode.", data: {…} }
400 only for a malformed request (missing pincode / non-digits / no state or city given).

`message` is ready to display as-is; `data` is where the pincode actually belongs, so the form can offer a correction. `cityChecked` tells you whether the city could be matched in our records at all — with strict:true an unverifiable city becomes invalid instead of being skipped.
